messages:
maria: FYI nightlies flagged a latency spike for a ~256-768 token cohort after yesterday's autotune tweak. looks like the probe scheduler backoff is biasing the kernel picker toward a slower midseq path. noticed on h100 and ampere pools. :eyes:

ben: Ugh. which test? microprobe or full kbench? any raw numbers?

maria: microprobe + kbench micro-agg. repro command I used: `./run_microprobe --arch h100 --seq-lens 256,512,768 --kernel-candidates v2-* --repeat 20`

ci-bot: nightly-run 2198765400 completed. 7 failures flagged: latency-regression (p95 > baseline + 12%), kernel-selection-mismatch. Report: https://ci/redwood/nightlies/2198765400 (logs attached)

jordan: pasted a trimmed log snippet:```
[2026-03-17T02:12:14Z] seq=512 picked kernel=v2_fuse_tile64_prefetch latency=9.8ms baseline=6.1ms
[2026-03-17T02:12:14Z] seq=512 kv_cache_hit=true batch=1
[2026-03-17T02:12:14Z] score: probe_backoff_penalty=0.7 kernel_score=1.2 final_score=0.84 -> pick v2_fuse_tile64_prefetch
```

ben: That penalty number looks off. We tuned backoff to 0.3 last week to avoid noisy probes causing flaps. 0.7 would heavily penalize low-throughput kernels, maybe overcompensating for cold-cache cases.

maya: I pushed the backoff heuristic change (PR #3852) that made penalty multiplicative and adaptive to recent probe variance. Could be our variance estimator is tiny for these midseqs so penalty jumps. linking PR: https://git/redwood/pr/3852

sam: Can we bisect which commit introduced the regression? I can schedule a bisect job on perf-lab. Prefer to run on ampere first (cheaper) then confirm on h100.

perf-bot: perf-bisect job queued: job-id=pb-7321. Targets: PRs merged between commit 9f2a and 2d4b. Will run microprobe 256/512/768 across archs. ETA ~45m.

jordan: quick local numbers (ampere, isolated):
- baseline kernel v1_tile32: p50=3.2ms p95=5.9ms
- chosen kernel v2_fuse_tile64_prefetch: p50=4.8ms p95=9.8ms
- KV cache warmups: cold cache adds ~1.1ms, but that doesn't explain 3-4ms delta

maria: Good data. Also noticed batching heuristics pick batch=1 for these probes because of continuous-batching heuristics observing high latency variance; might be interacting (small batch + wrong kernel = worse).

ben: Two separate levers: probe scheduler backoff (weights) and batching policy (threshold to pack into batch). Which changed recently?

maya: Autotune changed both: we changed pack_threshold from 2->3 for midseq to be conservative, and the backoff rule became multiplicative in PR #3852. They landed the same day. Could be a cross-effect.

sam: Bisect results: pb-7321 indicates the latency jump appears when PR 3852 landed. Reverting the multiplicative change in the backoff restores p95 to baseline.

maria: Ok. action items: 1) revert multiplicative backoff immediately in prod-nightly (short-term hotfix) 2) run a targeted microbench matrix isolating pack_threshold and backoff interaction 3) add a unit test in kpick CI to catch midseq mis-ranks 4) schedule a deeper KV-cache-aware probe simulation (maya/jordan)

ben: I'll open a rollback PR for the backoff change (will include toggles so we can flip on gradually).

maya: I'll collaborate on the probe sim. I want to instrument probe variance buckets and publish a small dashboard for the nightly to detect oscillations.

jordan: I'll add a kpick unit test that asserts kernel ranking monotonicity against a known microprobe dataset (256/512/768). Also will add a quick perf CI gate: if candidate pick increases p95 > baseline+8% mark as fail.

ci-bot: rollback PR created: https://git/redwood/pr/3869 (revert of PR #3852). CI started.

maria: Thanks team. Please post short updates here once rollback CI passes and after the targeted microbench. If nobody objects I'll land rollback once green. :thumbsup:

ben: I'll also run the repro on h100 after rollback to confirm.

jordan: note for followup: we should include KV cache temperature into the scoring function instead of only a binary hit flag; that would avoid penalizing kernels that perform well with warm cache. filing followup ticket.

maria: filed as infra/3814. Closing this thread for now; will re-open if rollback doesn't fix. :white_check_mark:
